No—under those conditions, you would not be able to spot the Moon.

Its altitude is about **−6.9°**, meaning it is nearly seven degrees below the true horizon. Even though it is **81.9% illuminated** and the sky is clear, an ordinary unaided observer cannot see an object that far below the horizon; the terrain and Earth itself block it. Civil twilight and the Moon’s brightness do not change that geometric obstruction.

It should become visible only after it rises above the local horizon—roughly when its altitude reaches 0°, subject to buildings, hills, and atmospheric refraction.
